rows: Maintain accounting records, systems, and financial reports
U.S. routine accounting records and financial reporting; conditional subset: SEC registrant annual or quarterly reports requiring officer certification and report signatures.

No task-wide human gate was found for routine accounting records or ordinary financial reports. SEC periodic filings create an Act-only conditional officer-certification and signature gate. Evidence: SIG-ACC01-ACQ-01; SIG-ACC01-INT-01; SIG-ACC01-DEC-01; SIG-ACC01-ACT-01.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
U.S. audit and assurance work; conditional subset: PCAOB-governed issuer or broker-dealer engagements.

PCAOB engagements require supervised and reviewed work, engagement-partner and engagement-quality review of judgments, concurring approval, and firm signature before report use. Other assurance settings are not generalized. Evidence: SIG-ACC02-ACQ-01; SIG-ACC02-INT-01; SIG-ACC02-DEC-01; SIG-ACC02-ACT-01; SIG-ACC02-ACT-02.
Provide financial planning, analysis, and decision support
U.S. routine FP&A, budgeting, forecasting, and management or client decision support; named transaction- or organization-specific approval regimes excluded.

No U.S.-wide legal or professional pre-effect human gate was found. Board, treasury, capital-allocation, or client approvals require a separately named scope and are not inferred here. Evidence: SIG-ACC03-ACQ-01; SIG-ACC03-INT-01; SIG-ACC03-DEC-01; SIG-ACC03-ACT-01.
Determine and document tax liabilities and filings
U.S. tax accounting and planning; conditional subset: preparation and paper or electronic submission of a federal tax return.

Tax research, calculation, and planning do not create a general approval gate. A filed federal return triggers taxpayer and, when applicable, paid-preparer signature or e-file authorization before transmission. Evidence: SIG-ACC04-ACQ-01; SIG-ACC04-INT-01; SIG-ACC04-DEC-01; SIG-ACC04-ACT-01; SIG-ACC04-ACT-02.
Deliver and sustain a software system or change
U.S. software delivery and maintenance; conditional subset: third-party software supplied for federal agency use under OMB M-22-18 and M-23-16.

No occupation-wide rule requires human approval of ordinary software stages. Covered third-party software for federal agency use requires a CEO/COO-signed secure-development attestation before agency use, creating an Act gate. Evidence: SIG-SWD01-ACQ-01; SIG-SWD01-INT-01; SIG-SWD01-DEC-01; SIG-SWD01-ACT-01.
Evaluate patients through diagnostic imaging and communicate findings
U.S. clinical diagnostic imaging in CMS-participating hospitals; research- and education-only use excluded; state licensure and privilege rules may add requirements.

CMS hospital rules separately require an authorized order, qualified-practitioner interpretation and clinical judgment, and an authenticated report. Evidence: SIG-RAD01-ACQ-01; SIG-RAD01-INT-01; SIG-RAD01-DEC-01; SIG-RAD01-ACT-01.
Plan and perform image-guided procedures and manage procedural care
U.S. clinical image-guided procedures in CMS-participating hospitals; research- and education-only use excluded; state licensure and facility privileges may add requirements.

CMS rules require an authorized order, qualified designated personnel, informed-consent controls for designated procedures, qualified procedural judgment, and authenticated documentation. Evidence: SIG-RAD02-ACQ-01; SIG-RAD02-INT-01; SIG-RAD02-DEC-01; SIG-RAD02-ACT-01.
Plan and deliver nuclear medicine diagnosis or therapy
U.S. clinical nuclear medicine in CMS-participating hospitals under NRC or Agreement State medical-use rules; research- and education-only use excluded.

CMS and NRC rules reserve ordering, interpretation, prescription or written-directive decisions, supervision, administration, and report authentication to authorized or qualified humans. Evidence: SIG-RAD03-ACQ-01; SIG-RAD03-INT-01; SIG-RAD03-DEC-01; SIG-RAD03-ACT-01.
U.S. project planning and coordination; conditional subset: covered paid renovation in pre-1978 housing or child-occupied facilities under EPA RRP.

General construction safety oversight does not create an ordinary planning approval gate. Covered lead renovation requires certified-renovator direction, specified presence, cleaning verification, and records. Evidence: SIG-CAN47203101-ACQ-01; SIG-CAN47203101-INT-01; SIG-CAN47203101-DEC-01; SIG-CAN47203101-ACT-01.
Construct, install, and restore permanent components
U.S. permanent construction and restoration; conditional subset: work involving asbestos-containing or presumed asbestos-containing material under 29 CFR 1926.1101.

Covered asbestos work assigns exposure assessment, hazard interpretation, control selection or certification, and on-site supervision to a trained competent person. Evidence: SIG-CAN47203102-ACQ-01; SIG-CAN47203102-INT-01; SIG-CAN47203102-DEC-01; SIG-CAN47203102-ACT-01.
Build temporary structures and site supports
U.S. temporary structures and site supports; conditional subset: a covered scaffold, ladder, formwork, shoring, or related regulated variant.

Covered scaffold, ladder, formwork, and shoring rules require qualified or competent-person inspection, interpretation, design or safety decisions, and supervision or pre-use approval. Evidence: SIG-CAN47203103-ACQ-01; SIG-CAN47203103-INT-01; SIG-CAN47203103-DEC-01; SIG-CAN47203103-ACT-01.
U.S. surface and interior-finish work; conditional subset: covered paid renovation disturbing painted surfaces in pre-1978 housing or child-occupied facilities under EPA RRP.

Covered lead renovation requires certified-renovator testing or documentation, lead determination, direction of work-practice decisions, specified presence, cleaning verification, and records. Evidence: SIG-CAN47203104-ACQ-01; SIG-CAN47203104-INT-01; SIG-CAN47203104-DEC-01; SIG-CAN47203104-ACT-01.
Transport and deliver freight by heavy truck
U.S. interstate heavy-truck freight covering conventional or SAE L0–3 human-operated CMVs and SAE L4–5 ADS-equipped CMVs within their ODD; state-only overlays excluded.

Human-operated CMV rules reserve checks, safety judgments, operation, and certifications to the driver. FMCSA permits the driver/operator concept to be satisfied without a human for SAE L4/L5 operation inside the ODD, so each human gate is conditional. Evidence: SIG-TRK01-ACQ-01; SIG-TRK01-ACQ-02; SIG-TRK01-INT-01; SIG-TRK01-INT-02; SIG-TRK01-DEC-01; SIG-TRK01-DEC-02; SIG-TRK01-ACT-01; SIG-TRK01-ACT-02.
SIG-TRK01-ACQ-01; SIG-TRK01-ACQ-02; SIG-TRK01-INT-01; SIG-TRK01-INT-02; SIG-TRK01-DEC-01; SIG-TRK01-DEC-02; SIG-TRK01-ACT-01; SIG-TRK01-ACT-02
Direct and coordinate organizational strategy and operations

U.S. general and operations management. Distinct role-bound endpoints such as SEC periodic-report certification by principal executive and financial officers and federal contract award by warranted contracting officers are outside this frozen general-management task; employer-specific approval policies and state or local rules require separate rows.

Federal labor and workplace rules constrain how managers obtain information and direct people, but do not reserve ordinary operating analysis, resource choices, or implementation to a named human approver. SEC certification and FAR contracting authority attach to different, explicitly role-bound outputs rather than this task's ordinary unit-management endpoint. Evidence: SIG-v01-MGR01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-MGR01-INT-01; SIG-v01-MGR01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-MGR01-ACT-01.
Administer recruitment, credentialing, and the employment relationship

U.S. recruitment, credential review, and employment administration; conditional subsets are procurement of an employment consumer report under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and completion of Form I-9 for a covered U.S. hire or reverification. State background-check, licensing, and employment rules require later jurisdiction rows.

FCRA employment screening requires the applicant's or employee's written permission before a consumer report is procured. Form I-9 separately requires an employer or authorized representative to inspect eligibility documents, determine that they reasonably appear genuine and relate to the employee, and sign the federal attestation. Federal equal-employment rules constrain, but do not reserve, the underlying hiring or credential-selection judgment to a human. Evidence: SIG-v01-HR01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-HR01-INT-01; SIG-v01-HR01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-HR01-ACT-01.

U.S. information-system and data safeguarding; conditional subset: a contractor or subcontractor information system subject to a currently implemented CMMC Level 1 or Level 2 self-assessment requirement under a DoD solicitation or contract. As of 2026-08-19, Phase II certification requirements are suspended while Phase I self-assessment requirements remain in place.

Current federal cybersecurity sources impose controls, assessment processes, and role responsibilities, but the present CMMC Phase I baseline does not assign ordinary security-input collection, vulnerability interpretation, or safeguard selection to a named human signatory. For a covered CMMC self-assessment, however, a senior Affirming Official must electronically attest in SPRS after assessment and annually thereafter. Evidence: SIG-v01-SEC01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-SEC01-INT-01; SIG-v01-SEC01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-SEC01-ACT-01.
Plan, design, and oversee civil engineering projects

U.S. federal civil-engineering baseline; conditional subset: a Plans, Specifications, and Estimates assembly for a Federal-aid highway project subject to approval under 23 CFR 630.205. State professional-engineering licensure, responsible-charge, seal, and exemption rules require later jurisdiction-specific rows.

The NCEES Model Law describes reserved professional-engineering practice but is not itself operative nationwide, so it cannot establish U.S.-baseline Interpret or Decide gates without a named adopting jurisdiction. A federal condition remains: 23 CFR 630.205 requires approval of the PS&E assembly before a covered Federal-aid highway project is advertised or begun by force account. Evidence: SIG-v01-CIV01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-CIV01-INT-01; SIG-v01-CIV01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-CIV01-ACT-02.
Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health
Investigate and address environmental hazards and impacts

U.S. environmental investigation, analysis, guidance, and harm-reduction work; conditional subsets are environmental information operations performed by or on behalf of EPA under the QAPP Standard and federal-agency public dissemination of influential scientific information under OMB M-05-03. QAPP emergency, police-power, and specified GLP exceptions and OMB bulletin exemptions remain applicable.

EPA's current QAPP Standard requires signed approval by operations and quality-assurance officials before covered environmental information gathering and before the selected project methods and quality plan are implemented. That plan approval does not validate each later scientific interpretation. Separately, OMB requires qualified-specialist peer review before a federal agency publicly disseminates influential scientific information; ordinary non-influential reports remain ungated. Evidence: SIG-v01-ENV01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-ENV01-INT-01; SIG-v01-ENV01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-ENV01-ACT-01.
Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health
Evaluate and administer environmental compliance and permitting

U.S. environmental compliance and permitting work; conditional subsets are environmental information operations performed by or on behalf of EPA under the QAPP Standard and final EPA-issued RCRA, UIC, PSD, or NPDES permit decisions under 40 CFR Part 124. Authorized state-program and other permit or enforcement regimes require separate jurisdiction rows.

For covered EPA environmental information operations, the QAPP Standard requires operations and quality-assurance signatures before gathering evidence and implementing the selected methods and quality plan, but it does not authenticate every compliance comparison. In the named Part 124 permit subset, the Regional Administrator must make and issue the final disposition and notify affected participants. Evidence: SIG-v01-ENV02-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-ENV02-INT-01; SIG-v01-ENV02-DEC-QA-01; SIG-v01-ENV02-DEC-PERMIT-01; SIG-v01-ENV02-ACT-01.
Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers
Assess, treat, and coordinate recovery support for clients

U.S. mental-health and substance-use social work; conditional subset: diagnosis and treatment furnished and billed as Medicare Part B clinical social work under 42 CFR 410.73. State clinical-social-work licensing, non-Medicare services, case management, and peer-support boundaries require later rows.

The Medicare rule does not reserve interviewing, record collection, resource lookup, or continuing-knowledge acquisition as a separately signed human output. For Medicare-covered diagnosis and treatment, it defines the provider as a state-licensed or certified clinical social worker with specified education and supervised experience and limits services to those the professional is legally authorized to perform. This condition applies to clinical interpretation, treatment planning, and treatment delivery, not every support activity. Evidence: SIG-v01-MSW01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-MSW01-INT-01; SIG-v01-MSW01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-MSW01-ACT-01.
Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers
Develop community prevention, policy, and service programs

U.S. community prevention, service-improvement, social-policy, and community-development research, design, implementation, and advice; excludes individual clinical diagnosis or treatment and any named grantor, legislature, regulator, employer, procurement, or community-board approval regime.

Federal clinical-social-work coverage is limited to individual diagnosis and treatment and therefore does not reserve this community-program task. Searches of federal clinical coverage, SAMHSA and public-health program surfaces, grant administration, and social-work professional authority found no U.S.-wide rule requiring a particular human role to approve community data collection, needs analysis, program or policy selection, implementation, or advisory communication. Named funder and government adoption gates are excluded and should receive separate rows. Evidence: SIG-v01-MSW02-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-MSW02-INT-01; SIG-v01-MSW02-DEC-01; SIG-v01-MSW02-ACT-01.
Analyze legal issues and advise clients

U.S. national-baseline legal-advisory work. State and territorial definitions of the practice of law, unauthorized-practice rules, admission requirements, and permitted nonlawyer services require later jurisdiction-specific rows.

ABA Model Rules 2.1, 5.3, and 5.5 guide lawyer conduct but neither define reserved legal practice nor operate as nationwide law. Without a named jurisdiction's adopted professional rule and operative unauthorized-practice authority, they do not establish a U.S.-baseline human gate on legal interpretation, advice selection, or delivery. Evidence: SIG-v01-LAW01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-LAW01-INT-01; SIG-v01-LAW01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-LAW01-ACT-01.
Develop and advocate cases in disputes and legal proceedings

U.S. dispute and proceeding work; conditional subset: papers presented in federal civil court under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 11 and advocacy in a forum requiring attorney admission. State-court, criminal, agency, settlement, and self-representation rules require separate rows.

No national rule reserves ordinary evidence collection to a lawyer. For a federal civil filing, however, Rule 11 requires a human attorney of record or unrepresented party to sign and, by presenting the paper, certify the factual and legal inquiry, contentions, and requested relief. Admission and unauthorized-practice rules also condition who may advocate for another in a tribunal. Evidence: SIG-v01-LAW02-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-LAW02-INT-01; SIG-v01-LAW02-DEC-01; SIG-v01-LAW02-ACT-01.

U.S. legislative, government-program, and enforcement-framework research, design, drafting, interpretation, and guidance preparation; excludes final legislative enactment, formal agency rule promulgation, and any named employer or chamber approval process.

The official House source states that members and committees are not required to use the Office of Legislative Counsel, even though House and Senate counsel offices provide attorney drafting services. The legislative votes, enrollment signatures, presidential action, agency approvals, and publication steps that make law or regulation effective fall outside this task's advisory and drafting endpoint. No general pre-effect human-authority gate was identified within the stated scope. Evidence: SIG-v01-LAW03-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-LAW03-INT-01; SIG-v01-LAW03-DEC-01; SIG-v01-LAW03-ACT-01.
Structure and administer legal transactions, instruments, estates, and fiduciary matters

U.S. national-baseline nonlitigation legal transactions, instruments, estates, ownership opinions, and fiduciary matters. State practice-of-law, instrument-execution, witnessing, notarization, probate, and fiduciary rules require later jurisdiction-specific rows.

ABA professional models do not themselves define or reserve transactional legal practice nationwide, and state rules differ across self-help documents, contracts, estates, probate, property, and fiduciary services. No U.S.-wide pre-effect human gate is assigned without a named operative jurisdiction. Evidence: SIG-v01-LAW04-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-LAW04-INT-01; SIG-v01-LAW04-DEC-01; SIG-v01-LAW04-ACT-01.
Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education

U.S. general elementary instruction and support; conditional subset: an IDEA initial evaluation, IEP development for a child who is or may be in the regular-education environment, and initial provision of special education or related services. Routine instruction and universal testing outside those triggers remain the baseline.

Routine classroom observation, grading, planning, and instruction do not carry a general federal signoff gate. IDEA creates named exceptions inside the frozen disability-access scope: parental informed consent before an initial evaluation, an IEP team including a regular teacher and an individual able to interpret evaluation implications, and parental consent before initial special-education services. Universal tests and review of existing data are expressly exempt from consent. Evidence: SIG-v01-TCH01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-TCH01-INT-01; SIG-v01-TCH01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-TCH01-ACT-01.
Deliver visual communication designs and production-ready content

U.S. graphic-design work across print, web, broadcast, and related media. Copyrightability, truth-in-advertising, and federal ICT accessibility requirements are included as searched substantive constraints; optional client or supervisor review and copyright registration do not establish a national pre-effect human-authority gate.

Copyright, advertising, and federal accessibility authorities regulate protectability and substantive conformance, but do not require an identified human to approve the brief, design analysis, creative choices, or production release. Human authorship can affect copyright protection without operating as signoff, and the FTC expressly does not pre-clear advertisements. Evidence: SIG-v01-GFX01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-GFX01-INT-01; SIG-v01-GFX01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-GFX01-ACT-01.
Provide and sustain nursing care and health improvement

U.S. registered-nursing care and health-improvement work; conditional subset: nursing services in a Medicare-participating hospital under 42 CFR 482.23. State nursing-practice acts, advanced-practice rules, anesthesia requirements, and nonhospital settings require later rows.

The federal hospital condition does not require separate human authorization before histories, symptoms, vital signs, test results, or operational inputs are collected. In Medicare-participating hospitals, it does require registered-nurse supervision and evaluation of each patient's nursing care, a current nursing care plan and human assignment of care, and licensed or supervised administration of drugs under authorized signed orders. Broader state and specialty variation is not generalized. Evidence: SIG-v01-RN01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-RN01-INT-01; SIG-v01-RN01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-RN01-ACT-01.

U.S. prehospital emergency response; conditional subset: ambulance service covered by 42 CFR 410.41 requiring specified human vehicle staffing and at least one appropriately certified and authorized EMT or paramedic. State EMS scope, protocol, and medical-control requirements require later rows.

The reviewed federal ambulance rules do not impose a distinct human gate on dispatch intake, scene interpretation, or the EMT's stabilization, destination, or emergency-transport decision. A physician certification for scheduled repetitive nonemergency transport governs Medicare coverage and scheduling rather than the frozen EMT decision endpoint. Covered ambulance vehicles still require specified human staffing, creating an Act condition. Evidence: SIG-v01-EMT01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-EMT01-INT-01; SIG-v01-EMT01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-EMT01-ACT-01.
Provide coordinated in-home health and daily-living support

U.S. in-home health and daily-living support; conditional subset: home health aide services furnished by a Medicare-certified home health agency under 42 CFR 484.80. Private-pay companionship, nonagency work, and state-only delegation rules require later rows.

The federal home-health rule requires aides to observe, record, recognize, and report changes, but it does not require a separate human approval before those observations or bounded recognitions occur. In a Medicare-certified agency, a registered nurse or other skilled professional assigns the patient and prepares written instructions, services must be ordered and included in a care plan, and aide work is supervised. These create conditional Decide and Act gates. Evidence: SIG-v01-HHA01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-HHA01-INT-01; SIG-v01-HHA01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-HHA01-ACT-01.
Provide public safety, law enforcement, and justice-process services

U.S. patrol and law-enforcement work; conditional subset: searches or seizures for which the Fourth Amendment and applicable warrant procedure require prior judicial authorization. Warrant exceptions, warrantless arrests, state civil-process rules, emergency aid, and administrative searches require separate treatment.

When a search or seizure requires a warrant, the Fourth Amendment and Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 41 require a neutral judge to determine probable cause, choose whether to authorize the intrusion, and issue the warrant before execution. That creates conditional Acquire, Interpret, Decide, and Act gates; ordinary warrantless policing and recognized exceptions remain outside the trigger. Evidence: SIG-v01-POL01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-POL01-INT-01; SIG-v01-POL01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-POL01-ACT-01.
Plan, prepare, cook, and release restaurant food

U.S. national-baseline restaurant-food production. The FDA Food Code is a model, and state, local, tribal, territorial, or federal adoptions, permits, HACCP-plan approvals, and variance regimes require later operative-jurisdiction rows.

The FDA Food Code describes approval of certain specialized-process HACCP plans, but it is a model rather than operative nationwide law and the current row cites no named adopting jurisdiction. Federal restaurant-facing sources do not impose a general pre-effect human gate on ordinary menu, preparation, cooking, sanitation, or release stages. Evidence: SIG-v01-COOK01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-COOK01-INT-01; SIG-v01-COOK01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-COOK01-ACT-01.
Janitors and Cleaners, Except Maids and Housekeeping Cleaners
Keep buildings and grounds clean, orderly, safe, and functional

U.S. national-baseline custodial building and grounds work. Specialized restricted-use-pesticide work is not treated as material to this SOC without occupation-setting evidence and should receive a later custodial-pesticide applicability row; ordinary cleaning, minor upkeep, snow, grounds, driving, and general-use pesticides are included.

EPA and OSHA rules do not impose a general pre-effect human gate on ordinary custodial intake, assessment, prioritization, or performance. Federal restricted-use-pesticide supervision is a real rule, but the reviewed evidence does not establish that noncertified RUP application is a recurring, non-incidental part of this janitorial occupation rather than pest-control-specialist work, so it is deferred to a separate applicability row. Evidence: SIG-v01-JAN01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-JAN01-INT-01; SIG-v01-JAN01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-JAN01-ACT-01.
Provide and support hair and cosmetology services

U.S. hair and cosmetology services at the national-baseline row; federal cosmetic-product and OSHA salon-safety rules are included, while state licensing, scope-of-practice, facility, and sanitation regimes require later jurisdiction-specific rows.

BLS confirms that state licensing is widespread, but qualifications and reserved scopes vary and do not establish one operative U.S.-wide stage rule. FDA expressly lacks authority over salon operation or cosmetology practice, and OSHA's product-hazard rules regulate workplace exposure rather than requiring client-by-client human approval. No national pre-effect gate was identified; state rows remain necessary. Evidence: SIG-v01-COS01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-COS01-INT-01; SIG-v01-COS01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-COS01-ACT-01.

U.S. national-baseline checkout and payment service. Federal-firearms-licensee transfer work is treated under the Retail Salespersons applicability row because current evidence does not establish it as a recurring, non-incidental cashier responsibility; ordinary purchases, payments, returns, refunds, and exchanges are included.

Ordinary checkout and payment have no identified U.S.-wide pre-effect human-authority gate. Federal firearm transfers do carry personal buyer and seller certifications, but the available evidence does not establish that licensed-dealer transfer responsibility is material to the Cashiers SOC rather than the Retail Salespersons task, where the condition is retained. Evidence: SIG-v01-CASH01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-CASH01-INT-01; SIG-v01-CASH01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-CASH01-ACT-01.
Sell merchandise and support customer purchases

U.S. retail merchandise sales and rentals; conditional subset: an over-the-counter firearm transfer by a federal firearms licensee to an unlicensed person under 18 U.S.C. 922 and 27 CFR 478.102 and 478.124. Statutory NICS and permit exceptions and stricter state or local firearm rules remain applicable.

Ordinary retail sales have no national human-signoff gate, but a federally licensed firearm transfer directly requires personal buyer certification, seller identity verification and NICS contact, an individual transferor's lawfulness judgment and certification, and a compliant release decision before the firearm may be transferred. The condition is limited to the regulated firearm subset and its exceptions. Evidence: SIG-v01-RET01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-RET01-INT-01; SIG-v01-RET01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-RET01-ACT-01.

U.S. customer-service intake, investigation, resolution, administration, and communication; conditional subset: outbound calls using an automatic telephone dialing system or artificial or prerecorded voice where 47 CFR 64.1200 requires the called party's prior express consent, including prior express written consent for covered advertising or telemarketing. Enumerated exceptions remain applicable.

Federal consumer-contact, privacy, billing, and telemarketing authorities regulate data handling and communication channels but do not require a named human to approve routine intake, case interpretation, or resolution selection. For covered automated or prerecorded outbound calls, however, the called party's prior consent is a documented pre-effect authorization, with written consent required for specified advertising or telemarketing calls. Evidence: SIG-v01-CSR01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-CSR01-INT-01; SIG-v01-CSR01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-CSR01-ACT-01.
Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
Provide coordinated office and administrative support

U.S. routine office and administrative support; conditional subsets: Department of Energy official employee travel requiring prior approval by a Travel Approving Official, and Department of Commerce ticket issuance after receipt of an approved travel authorization. Other agency travel, procurement, fiscal, privacy, and records policies require separate organizational rows.

Current federal records, privacy, travel, fiscal, and office-administration sources do not impose a general named-human gate on routine intake or administrative interpretation. Named federal travel workflows do: DOE requires a Travel Approving Official's prior approval, and Commerce generally withholds ticket issuance until an approved travel authorization is received, creating conditional Decide and Act gates for those agency subsets. Evidence: SIG-v01-ADM01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-ADM01-INT-01; SIG-v01-ADM01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-ADM01-ACT-01.
Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse
Produce, harvest, and prepare crops and plants

U.S. crop, nursery, and greenhouse production; conditional subset: a noncertified worker's use of a federally restricted-use pesticide under 40 CFR 171.201 in an applicable federal, state, tribal, or territorial certification program. Ordinary cultivation, harvest, packing, sale, delivery, and general-use pesticides remain the baseline.

Federal pesticide rules do not create a general signoff gate for crop observation, interpretation, or crop-protection selection. When a noncertified worker performs a covered restricted-use-pesticide application, 40 CFR 171.201 requires a certified applicator to ensure qualifications, provide use-specific instructions, and supervise performance; it does not separately reserve the underlying application-plan choice. Evidence: SIG-v01-FARM01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-FARM01-INT-01; SIG-v01-FARM01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-FARM01-ACT-01.
Install, maintain, and repair electrical systems

U.S. electrical installation, maintenance, and repair in OSHA-covered work; conditional subsets: qualified-person verification before equipment is treated as deenergized under 29 CFR 1910.333(b)(2)(iv), and work on or reenergization of exposed electrical parts under § 1910.333. State licensing, permits, inspections, and construction-code approvals require later jurisdiction rows.

OSHA does not impose a distinct human signoff on collecting specifications, measurements, fault reports, or material needs, nor a separate named approver for the electrician's ordinary work-plan choice. It does require a qualified person to test and verify deenergization before that finding is accepted, limits energized work to qualified persons, and requires qualified-person checks before reenergization. Evidence: SIG-v01-ELEC01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-ELEC01-INT-01; SIG-v01-ELEC01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-ELEC01-ACT-01.
Diagnose, maintain, and repair automotive vehicles

U.S. automotive diagnosis, maintenance, and repair; conditional subset: service for consideration involving refrigerant in a motor-vehicle air conditioner or MVAC-like appliance under 40 CFR 82.34. State repair-dealer licensing, inspection, and consumer-authorization programs require later jurisdiction rows.

The reviewed EPA and transportation-facing federal sources do not create a nationwide human gate for customer intake, vehicle diagnosis, estimates, ordinary service planning, or most mechanical and electrical repair. A named exception applies when paid service involves MVAC refrigerant: 40 CFR 82.34 requires an EPA-program-certified technician and approved equipment before that service may be performed. Evidence: SIG-v01-AUTO01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-AUTO01-INT-01; SIG-v01-AUTO01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-AUTO01-ACT-01.
Produce precision machined parts and instruments

U.S. precision machining and inspection of parts and instruments in general industry; OSHA machine-guarding and hazardous-energy rules are included, while contract-specific aerospace, defense, medical-device, customer, union, and employer quality approvals require separate named rows. Conditional subset: employee servicing or maintenance covered by 29 CFR 1910.147 where unexpected energization, startup, or stored-energy release could cause injury.

No nationwide human approval was identified for the task's requirements, analysis, work-plan selection, or completed product or repair. A bounded Act condition applies during covered servicing: 29 CFR 1910.147 requires an authorized employee to perform the energy-control sequence and verify isolation before precision machining setup or servicing proceeds. Contract-specific quality and release approvals remain outside the row. Evidence: SIG-v01-MACH01-ACQ-01; SIG-v01-MACH01-INT-01; SIG-v01-MACH01-DEC-01; SIG-v01-MACH01-ACT-01.
Build, modify, and repair machine tools or experimental assemblies

U.S. machine-tool maintenance and experimental assembly work in general industry; OSHA 1910.147 hazardous-energy control and 1910.212 guarding are included, while named employer, customer, laboratory, contract, and regulated-product release regimes require separate rows. U.S. retail bank teller transactions under the federal baseline; named bank dual-control policy, suspicious-activity escalation, vault access policy, and state law excluded.

U.S. non-police, non-fire, non-ambulance dispatch across utilities, repair, transport, delivery, and other field services; the operating sector and authority are not specified.

The occupation spans legally distinct transport, utility, service, and logistics regimes. The federal motor-carrier surface does not establish a stable human dispatch role for the entire frozen task, and a sector, carrier type, or named operating policy is required. U.S. heavy construction-equipment site work; conditional subset: covered excavation or trench work requiring competent-person inspection under 29 CFR 1926.651.

U.S. plumbing and piping installation or repair; conditional subset: paid work disturbing painted surfaces in pre-1978 housing or child-occupied facilities under EPA RRP.

U.S. transportation electrical/electronic installation and repair; conditional subset: aircraft maintenance and return-to-service work governed by 14 CFR part 43.

U.S. HVAC and refrigeration installation, commissioning, maintenance, and repair; conditional subset: stationary-equipment work requiring Section 608 technician certification.

U.S. interstate passenger transport by bus covering conventional or SAE Level 0–3 human-operated CMVs and qualifying SAE Level 4–5 ADS-equipped CMVs within their ODD; state transit and school-bus overlays excluded.

Conventional passenger-carrier rules reserve inspection, safety judgment, driving, and records to qualified drivers.
